tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run a JavaScript async-function body in a sandbox that calls tools synchronously; only console.log output and the return value come back. Use for batch work (loops, grep+aggregate, edits). timeoutMs is the whole-program timeout (default 300000 ms, max 1800000). root:"D:/abs/dir" makes relative paths, path-less glob/grep and cwd-less bash use that existing absolute directory (tools.root exposes it). Paths: relative to cwd (or root). On big trees give glob/grep a path or specific pattern. Errors carry .code/.nextAction and "[CODE]" prefix: INVALID_ARGUMENT NOT_FOUND NOT_UNIQUE COUNT_MISMATCH STALE LOCKED EXISTS POLICY_DENIED BUSY OUTPUT_LIMIT RG_UNAVAILABLE RESULT_UNKNOWN. tools.read({path,offset?,limit?,numbered?}) (numbered:true -> "N: text" lines with real line numbers). tools.revision({path}) -> 16-hex sha256 prefix of the file content; pass it as expectedRevision to tools.edit (or as {path: revision} to tools.replace) to get STALE and write nothing if the content changed since (works across run_code calls). tools.write({path,content}); tools.edit({path,old,new,all?,expect?,expectedRevision?}) -> {replaced,lines} (atomic; the mtime STALE check still applies only if this same program read the file first; expectedRevision adds a cross-call content check; revision-guarded writes also take a cross-process lock (one writer at a time; LOCKED after ~2 s, a lock left by a crash is taken over after 30 s); with all:true pass expect:<count you mean to change>, a different count writes nothing and throws COUNT_MISMATCH). tools.glob({pattern?:string|string[],path?,sort?:"path"|"modified",details?,offset?,limit?=5000}) and tools.grep({pattern,path?,glob?,ignoreCase?,outputMode?:"content"|"files_with_matches"|"count",before?,after?,multiline?,offset?=0,limit?=500}) -> {items,total,complete,nextOffset} (ripgrep: .gitignore honoured; skips hidden, node_modules, target, .venv, files>2MB). glob items: path, or {path,size,mtime} with details. grep items: {file,line,text<=300} (+uncounted context:true rows), {file,count}, or paths. tools.replace({pattern(JS regex; lookaround, \1, named groups ok),replacement($1 ok),path?,glob?,flags?,dryRun?,maxReplacements?,expect?,expectedRevision?}) -> {files,matches,changed,items:[{file,count,lines}],dryRun} (expect: total matches you mean to change; a different count writes nothing and throws COUNT_MISMATCH). Any write that changed several places is listed at the top of the output with its line numbers: check each one was intended. tools.batch({action:"plan"|"run"|"resume"|"list",operations:[{op:"copy"|"move"|"remove",path,to?}],protect?:string[],root?,toRoot?,id?}): root-relative "/" paths (to is relative to toRoot if given: another dir/drive), <=512 ops, no overwrite, destination parent must exist, no links, protect untouched; preflighted first. plan only journals; run needs operations; resume takes only id (unknown items: checked, not redone); list shows jobs. -> {id,status:"completed"|"partial"|"failed"|"planned",done,failed,unknown,total,detailsRef}. tools.bash({command,cwd?,timeoutMs?,env?,background?})->{code,stdout,stderr}; background:true returns {id} immediately, then tools.job({id,wait?,tailChars?=4000})->{done,code,stdout,stderr} (jobs survive run_code calls; 2h cap). await tools.parallel([{command,cwd?,timeoutMs?,env?}],{concurrency?=4,<=16}) runs <=64 bash calls -> [{code,stdout,stderr,timedOut?}] in order. Child processes default to PYTHONUTF8=1 and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8; an explicit env wins. tools.test({command,workdir?,timeoutMs?=300000,maxFailures?=10}) runs a test command through the same bash path -> {status:"passed"|"failed"|"error"|"timeout"|"unknown",exitCode,counts?,failures,tail?,error?,outputPath} (pytest/vitest/jest/node --test parsed conservatively): print that summary instead of piping test output; when status is "error", read error and tail, and outputPath is the path to the full output (read it with tools.read). ref.put(v)->id; ref.page(id,{offset,limit,fields,equals,maxBytes=16384})->{total,offset,items,nextOffset,complete,omitted} (OUTPUT_LIMIT if one row exceeds maxBytes; also reads detailsRef); ref.text(id,{from,to}) returns a slice of the saved text; ref.release(id). Refs: per session, 24h. Output over ~8000 chars (or maxChars, <=50000) keeps about the first 70% and last 30% (cut on line boundaries); the marker names the omitted output lines and the exact ref.text(id,{from,to}) call that returns them

script: tool.call Bash rm -rf build && git push --force origin main

notes: ./register.ts env reads: PTC_RUN_DSH_READ_LIMIT, PTC_RUN_READONLY, PTC_RUN_RO_AGENTS, PTC_RUN_RO_ROOTS, PTC_RUN_SDK_IN_PROMPT
